originality.rationale: The leading 2016 source defines strong non-overlapping codes without finding this optimum; the most directly relevant 2024 paper explicitly poses the minimum-mean-length question, while its bounds do not imply 16/3. The published finite fixed-length construction only implies upper bound 18. Actual published-finding corpus searches identify fixed-length binary and variable-length ternary near neighbors, not the present exact claim.
residual_risks: No search establishes global historical uniqueness; an older unindexed finite enumeration could contain the same result.
Bilotta uses both weak and strong conventions; this result explicitly requires the latter.

value.rationale: This determines the first nontrivial binary three-message instance of the natural minimum-average-length problem explicitly posed in Wang–Wang 2024. The strict reduction from fixed length six to mean 16/3 and exhaustive classification of four optimal solutions provide a meaningful synchronization-code design threshold.
